newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius EPZ earnings threatened by strong rupee.
newsitem.headline: Mauritius EPZ earnings threatened by strong rupee.

text.p: Earnings in the Mauritian Export Processing Zone (EPZ) sector are threatened mainly by a strong rupee policy, industry leaders said on Tuesday.

Mauritius Export Processing Zone Association (MEPZA) Chairman Francois De Grivel told Reuters in an interview on Tuesday that currency fluctuations were also a major obstacle in forecasting volume of exports for 1997.

The EPZ sector is the largest sectoral employer in Mauritius with 79,447 employees working in EPZ enterprises in December 1996 against 80,466 in December 1995. The EPZ sector consisted of 477 enterprises as at December 1996 against 481 in 1996.

The EPZ sector is 85 percent textile oriented and the MEPZA is recommending for more investment in non-textile fields, such as informatics, electronics and electronics products, electro-mechanics, light engineering, pharmaceutical products, editing and printing and plastic and rubber products.
He saw earnings at 21 billion rupees in 1997 from an estimate of 21.5 billion rupees in 1996 and 18.3 billion rupees in 1995, and zeroed on a strong rupee as impeding higher earnings.
The Mauritian rupee eased from May to October 1996, falling to an average of commercial rate of 20.70 rupees versus the dollar in mid-October from 19.6285 at end-May.
Over the past six months, central bank interventions provided support for the local currency which strengthened to the region of 19.80 rupees to the dollar in early February.
De Grivel said industrialists were wondering about how far the central bank would go in supporting the rupee.
"MEPZA members need to know more on how the central bank is handle the currrencies' basket. They want to have access to more information and set proposals accordingly," he said.
The MEPZA and ministry of industry and commerce will start working on a strategic plan for the medium and long term future of the manufacturing sector in April, De Grievel said.
At a recent meeting with EPZ operators, Industry and Commerce Minister Jayen Cuttaree asked the EPZ to redefine its future and its relationship with the government.
"We are deeply conscious that... Mauritius is vulnerable to negative impacts deriving from fierce competitions at international level," De Grievel said.
He suggested that MEPZA should fully participate in the re-engineering of the EPZ sector and the review of the EPZ Act and the Industrial Expansion Act as proposed by Cuttaree.

MEPZA would also organise QUENVEX 97 (Quality Environment Conference cum Exhibition) in July and would launch a QUENVEX Award to recognise companies making special efforts to demonstrate an environmental responsibility.
"The QUENVEX Award will provide opportunity for the Mauritian enterprises to keep in touch with international trend on environmental issues," De Grivel said.

He said MEPZA was pursuing its awareness campaign in favour of a textile upmarket industry and for more diversification in the manufacturing sector: "We must develop a spirit of competitiveness within productivity, total quality products in the shortest delivery delay process by a growing productivity."
